content.introduction: Determining whether now is a good time to invest depends on various factors, including financial goals, risk tolerance, and market conditions. The sources suggest that long-term investing often yields positive outcomes, with the S&P 500 having positive annual returns in over 75% of the past 20 years and an average annual return of about 11%. However, the sources also note that investing requires careful planning, research, and the ability to adapt, as stocks can be volatile and fall for months at a time. The sources do not provide a definitive answer but emphasize the importance of individual assessment and expert advice.
body:
Determining whether now is a good time to invest depends on an array of factors, including your financial goals, risk tolerance, and current market conditions. While volatility can evoke uncertainty, history shows that long-term investing often yields positive outcomes. [...] Investing in the market requires a careful assessment of various factors, including economic conditions, interest rates, and overall market sentiment. You should analyze current economic indicators such as inflation rates, unemployment figures, and GDP growth to gauge the health of the economy. Understanding the Federal Reserve’s monetary policy can also provide insights into future interest rate changes, which significantly impact investment strategies. [...] In the end, investing in the market requires careful planning, research, and the ability to adapt. By understanding market indicators, diversifying your investments, and possibly seeking expert advice, you can make informed decisions that enhance your financial future.

Whether now is a good time to invest is ultimately a question that rests on your unique situation and perspective.

Long term investments are essential for most individuals to meet their financial goals — assuming the investments are carefully selected as part of a diversified portfolio. But the thought of losing money can be scary and it's natural to worry whether now is a good time to invest. [...] Considering the market’s best days tend to occur during periods of heightened volatility, it’s another reason why “get invested and stay invested” is a good strategy to consider for a majority of investors.5

But let’s take it a step further: What if you had the worst-possible timing? [...] From 1936 through 2025, the U.S. stock market never had negative returns on a rolling 20-year basis. And since 1972, the S&P 500 hasn’t had negative returns on any rolling timeframe longer than 12 years.1
 In the past 20 years, the S&P 500 had an average intra-year decline of nearly 15%. Yet the index had positive annual returns in over 75% of those years.2

Over those same 20 years, the average annual return of the S&P 500 was about 11%.3
